purpose: Evaluate the same isolated BugBank-versus-plain procedure on six additional recent, source-verifiable open problems without selecting problems for an expected arm outcome. This v2 record corrects the pool before launch after primary evidence showed that one unselected v1 item was already resolved.

confirmatory_boundary.policy: These exploratory problems and results must never alter, replace, or be pooled into the frozen comparison of 58 paired protocol observations. Those observations cover 36 distinct source targets because 22 are explicit continuations of targets in the original 31. Any expanded aggregate must be reported only as a separately labeled exploratory aggregate alongside the unchanged confirmatory result.

discovery.disclosure: An initial web discovery search occurred before this file was written. No new-candidate solver run, audit run, BugBank retrieval, or arm outcome was inspected. The exact discovery procedure is frozen here before further source search.
ordered_queries: site:drops.dagstuhl.de 2025 open problems graph algorithms report
discovery.result_depth: Capture the top five results per query in the order returned on 2026-09-03. Within each query, take the first direct source document satisfying source-level eligibility. Deduplicate by canonical document identifier.
allowed_source_types: An author-uploaded primary paper expressly compiling named or numbered open problems.
An official Dagstuhl seminar report expressly collecting open problems.
source_exclusions: Search snippets without an accessible full source.
Broad challenge or agenda reports that do not state exact problems.

include_all: The source is dated 2024-01-01 through the source cutoff date.
The latest accessible source version explicitly presents the item as open.
The item is an exact truth-valued theorem or conjecture, or a fully specified binary complexity claim.
A proof or disproof can settle the exact item.
All definitions and context needed to state the target can be preserved without relying on a figure, private data, software, or unbounded external reconstruction.
The item is nontrivial and not a semantic duplicate of a target in the frozen confirmatory comparison or another eligible pool item.
exclude_any: Determine, find, best-possible, or classify prompts lacking a source-stated exact target.
Multipart research agendas or empirical engineering questions.
Items already resolved or explicitly marked as having progressed to resolution in the latest accessible source/status check.
Ambiguous statements whose domain or quantifiers cannot be recovered exactly.
eligibility.pool_freeze: Freeze the complete eligible pool and a reasoned exclusion ledger before any BugBank access or solver/model call.

selection.digest_rule: Compute lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of seed_prefix followed immediately by canonical_key, with no newline.
selection.ordering: Sort ascending by (digest, canonical_key) and select the first six eligible items. If fewer than six are eligible, select all and report the shortfall.
selection.replacement_policy: No substitution is allowed after any arm outcome. If an item is later found ineligible or already solved, invalidate the exploratory cohort unless the correction occurs before launch and selection is rerun from a newly versioned, fully frozen pool.
forbidden_criteria: BugBank relevance or expected retrieval usefulness.
Proof shape chosen to favor either arm.
Any solver, audit, or retrieval output.

versioned_continuation_policy.trigger: every validated nonterminal arm-problem cell at the current 50-iteration block cap
versioned_continuation_policy.selection: all and only triggered cells, selected mechanically without regard to problem identity, arm, apparent progress, retrieval content, or paired outcome
versioned_continuation_policy.continuation_run_id_rule: open_frontier_paired_exploratory_unbiased_v2_continuation_v<N>_20260904, where N starts at 1 and increases by one for every required block
versioned_continuation_policy.continuation_iteration_rule: version N runs exactly the next block of at most 50 iterations: 50*N+1 through 50*(N+1)
versioned_continuation_policy.starting_state: the exact byte-bound last revision, audit, token totals, and BugBank receipt history of that cell from the preceding validated version
versioned_continuation_policy.stopping_rule: stop a continued cell immediately at its first strict independently audited full solution or its first protocol-valid INCONCLUSIVE_FIXED_POINT endpoint
versioned_continuation_policy.plain_budget_rule: retain WHOLE_PROOF_FIRST_SOLUTION_V1 incremental BugBank-token endpoint matching for every continued plain cell
versioned_continuation_policy.versioning_rule: repeat mechanically in successive separately preregistered and runtime-sealed 50-iteration versions until every cell is terminal; already-terminal cells remain frozen and are never rerun

requirements: Use disjoint run, operations, and scratch roots.
Freeze source snapshots, normalized targets, semantic audits, problem IDs, BugBank database identity, schemas, prompts, runtime payload, and runtime seal before launch.
Stop either arm immediately at its first strict audited full solution.
For an inconclusive plain arm, enforce the protocol's incremental BugBank-token endpoint matching rule.

Continue every validated nonterminal arm-problem cell at each 50-iteration cap in mechanically selected, separately preregistered and runtime-sealed 50-iteration versions until it reaches VERIFIED_FULL or INCONCLUSIVE_FIXED_POINT; never rerun already-terminal cells.
Require the independent validator to report VALID_COMPLETE before reporting results.

outcome_access_attestation: At the corrected v2 freeze, the v1 run had never been created, no solver, auditor, model, or BugBank retrieval had been run for any candidate, and no arm outcome for the new cohort existed.
